svg.text: Pick a floor plan and the planner lays out furniture, prices the set, and works out which bed suits each bedroom and where it goes. The bed rules are real arithmetic, ported
from the Bed Fit project; the room sizes are typical for the plan type, not measured from a real flat.
1 RK, 1 BHK, 2 BHK or 3 BHK. Each is a fixed 2D schematic
A hardcoded furniture bundle for that plan (lib/planner.ts).
Rent monthly or buy; drop pieces; add the set to the cart.
Every bedroom drawn to scale with the bed placed, walkways
The same four schematics drive the plan picker, listing thumbnails and the locator that shows which

wins: a door is worse than a doorway,

width. The bed is centred in whatever

One good side beats two bad
If both sides would be under 1′6″, the
bed is pushed 0′6″ off the far wall so
the entry side keeps a real walkway.
2′0″ past the foot. Fits, but tight:
anything less. Does not fit: it will

The 2 BHK, as the planner draws it
Headboard on the bottom wall. 1′10″ each side, 5′4″ past the foot,
a side table on each side.
Only the left wall is clear. The door swing takes the bottom 3 ft,
so the queen centres in the 8 ft left: 1′6″ each side.
A king goes in, but pushed off the far wall: 1′2″ on one side,
0′6″ on the other. Shown in red on the drawing.
